# Story 14.2: Implement the unified per-domain error mapper and delete local duplicates

Status: ready-for-dev

## Story

As a developer,
I want one shared per-domain error mapper wired into every Fastify route in `apps/server` with the hand-rolled local handlers deleted,
So that all failure responses are produced through a single helper — no more inconsistent 503/500 shapes or duplicated local logic (P0 item #1 from Aspect 9 of the critical review).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Story 14.1's red-phase tests pass: `universe/index.ts` and `universe/add-symbol/index.ts` delegate their failure responses to one shared per-domain error mapper, with no hand-rolled local handler remaining in either file.
2. `health/index.ts` produces its 503/500 failure shapes through the same shared per-domain error mapper rather than inline hand-built response objects.
3. Behavioral preservation: for each route (`universe`, `add-symbol`, `health`), a representative failure yields the same status code and response body as before unification — no client-visible change.
4. The previously-skipped tests from Story 14.1 are unskipped (`.skip()` removed) and pass under `nx test server`; the full server suite is green with no pre-existing test modified, weakened, or removed.

## Tasks / Subtasks

- [ ] Task 1 (AC: #1–#3): Remove skip markers and confirm red.
  - [ ] 1.1 In the specs added by Story 14.1, remove every `it.skip` marker and run `nx test server`, confirming the new assertions FAIL against current code (red).
- [ ] Task 2 (AC: #1): Extract one shared per-domain error mapper.
  - [ ] 2.1 Create/extend a single per-domain error-mapper function in `apps/server/src/app/middleware/create-error-response.function.ts` (or a sibling util) that maps a domain failure to the canonical status code + body shape used across routes.
- [ ] Task 3 (AC: #1): Wire `universe` and `add-symbol` to the shared mapper; delete local duplicates.
  - [ ] 3.1 In `apps/server/src/app/routes/universe/index.ts`, replace the hand-rolled failure handler with a call to the shared mapper.
  - [ ] 3.2 In `apps/server/src/app/routes/universe/add-symbol/index.ts`, do the same and delete its local duplicate handler.
- [ ] Task 4 (AC: #2): Wire `health` to the shared mapper; remove inline shapes.
  - [ ] 4.1 In `apps/server/src/app/routes/health/index.ts`, replace the inline 503/500 response objects with calls to the shared mapper.
- [ ] Task 5 (AC: #3, #4): Verify behavioral preservation and green suite.
  - [ ] 5.1 Confirm each route's representative failure still yields the same status code + body as before unification.
  - [ ] 5.2 Run `nx test server` and confirm fully green with Story 14.1's tests now passing (unskipped).

## Dev Notes

- **Why:** three error-handling styles currently coexist in `apps/server` — `create-error-response.function.ts` (middleware only), hand-rolled local handlers in `universe/index.ts` and `universe/add-symbol/index.ts`, and inline 503 shapes in `health/index.ts`. Unifying on one per-domain mapper removes a whole class of inconsistent failure responses.
- **Behavioral preservation is the contract:** the shared mapper must reproduce each route's existing status codes and bodies exactly. Do not "improve" or normalize response shapes beyond what already exists — that would be a client-visible change outside this story's scope.
- **First task is always unskip → confirm red → implement.** The red-phase tests from Story 14.1 define the target; do not edit their assertions to make them pass, only the production code.
- Vitest is the workspace test framework; server tests run via `nx test server`.

### Project Structure Notes

- Modify: `apps/server/src/app/routes/universe/index.ts`, `apps/server/src/app/routes/universe/add-symbol/index.ts`, `apps/server/src/app/routes/health/index.ts` (delegate to shared mapper, delete local duplicates).
- Create/modify: the shared per-domain error-mapper function in `apps/server/src/app/middleware/create-error-response.function.ts` or a sibling util under `apps/server/src/app/utils/`.
- Modify: Story 14.1's specs (remove `.skip()` markers only — no assertion changes).
